# GLOBAL SETTINGS (Apply to all formats)
jupyter: python3
toc: true
number-sections: true
highlight-style: github

# EXECUTION OPTIONS
execute:
  echo: true          # Show code? (Set to false for final executive reports)
  warning: false      # Hide warnings
  message: false      # Hide package loading messages
  cache: false        # Set to true if calculations take a long time
  fig-dpi: 300        # image export resolution
  fig-width: 6        # default figure width (inches)
  fig-height: 4       # default figure height
  fig-format: png     # choose png/pdf/svg
  fig-align: center   # center figures
  echo-fenced: true   # ensure fenced code is shown nicely

# FORMAT-SPECIFIC SETTINGS (which comes first gets rendered)
format:
  # 1. HTML
  html:
    theme: cosmo      # Options: cosmo, journal, flatly, sketchy
    toc-location: left
    code-fold: true   # Collapses code blocks! Readers click to see code.
    code-tools: true  # Adds a "Code" menu to show/hide all code
    embed-resources: true # Creates a single self-contained .html file
    fig-width: 8
    fig-height: 6
    smooth-scroll: true
    anchor-sections: true

  # 2. PDF
  pdf:
    documentclass: scrartcl
    classoption: [landscape] # Remove this line for standard Portrait orientation
    papersize: a4
    geometry:
      - top=20mm
      - left=20mm
      - right=20mm
      - bottom=20mm
    colorlinks: true    # Makes TOC and citations clickable blue links
    fig-pos: "H"        # Forces figures to stay exactly where you put them
    lof: true           # Generate List of Figures?
    lot: true           # Generate List of Tables?
    mainfont: "TeX Gyre Pagella" # Professional font (optional, requires installation)
    monofont: "Consolas"      # Code font
    include-in-header:	# This helps to add a gray box behind codechunks
      text: |
        \usepackage{xcolor}
        \usepackage{framed}
        \definecolor{shadecolor}{RGB}{230,230,230}  % Light grey color
        \renewenvironment{Shaded}{\begin{snugshade}}{\end{snugshade}}


    
# CROSS-REFERENCING (Critical for scientific reports)
# Allows you to use @fig-name in text
crossref:
  fig-title: Figure
  tbl-title: Table
  title-delim: ":"

#| label: setup
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# --- 1. System & Environment ---
import os
import sys
import warnings

# Filter out messy warnings for a clean report
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

# --- 2. Data Manipulation ---
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# --- 3. Visualization ---
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Configure plotting style 
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="paper", palette="viridis")
plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'] = (10, 6)
plt.rcParams['figure.dpi'] = 120  # High resolution for print
plt.rcParams['savefig.bbox'] = 'tight'

# Configure Pandas display
pd.set_option('display.max_columns', None)  # Show all radiomic features
pd.set_option('display.precision', 4)       # Clean decimal formatting

# --- 4. Machine Learning Imports ---
# Preprocessing
from sklearn.model_selection import (
    train_test_split, 
    StratifiedKFold, 
    GridSearchCV, 
    cross_val_score
)
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, RobustScaler
from sklearn.feature_selection import SelectKBest, f_classif, RFECV

# model
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier, GradientBoostingClassifier
from sklearn.svm import SVC
from xgboost import XGBClassifier

# evaluate
from sklearn.metrics import (
    accuracy_score, 
    confusion_matrix, 
    classification_report, 
    roc_auc_score, 
    roc_curve,
    ConfusionMatrixDisplay
)

# --- 5. random seed ---
# Use this variable everywhere you need a random_state
random_seed = 42

print("Setup Complete. Libraries loaded, plotting style configured and random seed set.")
